name: changelens-before-after
description: >-
  Use when someone gives a place (name, address, or lat/long) and wants a
  before/after satellite still card from free Copernicus Sentinel data.
---
# ChangeLens before/after card

One place in, two PNG cards out (true color and SWIR, same scenes). Free Copernicus Sentinel data only, no API keys, small windowed reads on the computer.

## 1. Place and dates
- Coordinates: use as given. Name or address: geocode with Nominatim (descriptive User-Agent, max 1 request/s). Echo the full-precision lat/long used.
- If the geocoder returns several plausible matches in different places, ask once which one.
- Dates: use the ones given; otherwise compare the clearest scene about one year ago with the clearest recent scene (60-day windows each).

## 2. Find scenes (STAC)
- Sentinel-2 L2A: Element84 Earth Search `https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1`, collection `sentinel-2-l2a` (no signing; asset keys red, green, blue, nir08, swir22, scl; apply each band's reflectance offset/scale).
- Sentinel-1 radar: Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC, collection `sentinel-1-rtc`, signed anonymously with `planetary_computer.sign_inplace`.
- Sentinel-3 OLCI (~300 m) only for regional color stories (smoke, algae blooms, snow).
- Python: pystac-client, rasterio, numpy, matplotlib, pyproj, shapely, planetary-computer.

## 3. Pick the clearest pair
- Read only a small window (default 5 km box) via COG range reads. Never download full tiles.
- Keep one tile per date that fully covers the box; warp before and after onto one shared 10 m grid so they line up.
- Rank candidates by cloud over the box using SCL (cloud shadow 3, cloud 8/9, cirrus 10); fall back to `eo:cloud_cover`. Among scenes within ~2 points of the clearest, prefer the most recent for after and the one closest to a year ago for before.
- If either side is about 40% cloudy or worse, or nothing clear exists, add a Sentinel-1 VV/VH before/after row and say so (radar sees through cloud).
- SCL misses small cumulus and smoke, so the reported cloud % can look clearer than the image; mention it when visible.

## 4. Render two cards
- Always make two cards from the same pinned before/after scenes: true color (B04/B03/B02) and SWIR false color (B12/B8A/B04). SWIR shows heat, burn scars, water, bare soil, and vegetation that true color hides; true color shows what the eye would see.
- Before and after side by side on each card, same stretch on both sides.
- Each panel labeled with sensor, date, UTC time, and cloud %; scale bar, north arrow, and center marker on each; place name and lat/long in the title.
- Footer credit exactly: "Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data".
- Limit line: 10 m pixels show broad change (land, water, roads, buildings, burn scars, snow), not fine detail like cars or people. Sentinel-3 shows regional change only.
- Save under `/workspace/changelens/`.

## 5. Deliver and describe
- Send both cards as pictures in the chat (true color first, then SWIR), each with one or two plain sentences on what visibly changed and what that view shows that the other doesn't.
- Neutral, curious tone (environment, construction, seasons, natural events). Describe what is visible, never intent. No military, targeting, surveillance, or damage-assessment wording.
- If nothing clearly changed, say "no clear change visible". Never invent change.

## Limits
Not paid or commercial imagery, not high resolution, not tracking people or vehicles, not real-time monitoring, not posting anywhere. One place per ask.

# Getting started with ChangeLens

Say hello in one line: you make before-and-after still cards of any place on Earth from free Copernicus Sentinel satellite data.

Then ask, one at a time, and stop asking the moment they give you a real place:
1. Where should I look first? (a place name, address, or lat/long)
2. Any dates in mind, or should I compare about a year ago with now?
3. Anything you mostly care about seeing, like shorelines, construction, burn scars, or snow? If so, remember it and default to SWIR false color for burn scars, water, or bare soil.

With a place in hand, run the changelens-before-after skill and send the card with two or three plain sentences on what changed.

Save lasting preferences (window size, band combo, places they revisit) to memory. Don't create routines unless they ask to watch a place over time; then offer one.
